column1: # Default public DNS resolver database for dns-speedtest.
# Format (TAB-separated):
#   enabled  provider  ip  service_type  filtering  notes  source
# enabled: 1/0, yes/no, true/false
# Filtering resolvers are labeled and disabled by default so they are not
# silently compared as equivalent to unfiltered resolvers.
# IPv6 rows are accepted by the parser; bundled defaults that are enabled
# are IPv4 for predictable out-of-the-box operation.
# Addresses verified against official provider documentation on 2026-08-16.
# See docs/SOURCES.md.
# --- Cloudflare Public DNS (https://developers.cloudflare.com/1.1.1.1/ip-addresses/) ---
# Three product categories: unfiltered (1.1.1.1), malware (1.1.1.2), family (1.1.1.3).
# Secondaries and IPv6 stay disabled; they are the same anycast services.

column6: 1.1.1.1 for Families: block malware and adult content
1.1.1.1 for Families secondary: malware and adult content

column1: # --- Google Public DNS (https://developers.google.com/speed/public-dns/docs/using) ---
# --- Quad9 (https://quad9.net/service/service-addresses-and-features/) ---
# 9.9.9.9 is Quad9's default service: malware/phishing blocklist + DNSSEC.

column6: Quad9 default: malware/phishing blocklist, DNSSEC, no ECS
Quad9 unsecured: no blocklist, no DNSSEC (experts)

column1: # --- Cisco OpenDNS (https://www.opendns.com/setupguide/) ---
# Consumer OpenDNS Home nameservers include phishing protection.
# --- AdGuard Public DNS (https://adguard-dns.io/en/public-dns.html) ---
# Default AdGuard DNS blocks ads/trackers. The non-filtering server is the
# fair general-purpose comparison target and is enabled by default.

column6: AdGuard Default: block ads, trackers, malware, phishing
AdGuard Family protection: ads + adult content + Safe Search

column1: # --- TurkNet ISP DNS ---
# Commonly published TurkNet recursive address (AS12735). This is an ISP
# resolver, not a global public anycast product like 1.1.1.1 / 8.8.8.8.
